facts.statement: version 0.5.144 of tensorlake was published to npm using a compromised maintainer account.
the package carries valid npm provenance.
Only the npm package was affected, the PyPI and crates.io tensorlake packages and the tensorlake CLI were not.
executed during package installation via a preinstall hook.
The payload also installs a persistent service named gh-token-monitor that deletes the user's home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked .
Remove it before rotating any GitHub token
Version 0.5.143 and all prior versions are unaffected.

editorial.title: TensorLake's npm release workflow published credential-stealing 0.5.144
editorial.summary: TensorLake says a compromised maintainer account pushed malicious code into its repository and published tensorlake 0.5.144 through its own npm workflow. An install hook harvested credentials, and the package carried valid provenance. TensorLake says its PyPI, crates.io and CLI distributions were unaffected.
editorial.why_it_matters: A reported monitor could delete a user's home directory after GitHub token revocation. Valid provenance did not make this release trustworthy.
editorial.action: Check lockfiles for tensorlake 0.5.144. If installed with scripts enabled, follow TensorLake's containment order: isolate the host, remove the reported monitor before revoking tokens, then rotate credentials from a clean system.
